quarterly_data.signal: Full-year 2025 results: ongoing earnings of $3.80 per share versus $3.50 per share in 2024, the twenty-first consecutive year of meeting or exceeding initial ongoing guidance; GAAP earnings were $3.42 per share after a $300 million (38¢ per share) charge for the Marshall Wildfire settlement in principle. CFO Brian Van Abel: higher electric and natural gas revenues (rate case outcomes, nonfuel riders and sales growth, net of fuel and purchased power) added $1.21 per share and higher AFUDC added 27¢ per share, offset by higher interest charges and common equity financing (46¢ per share, funding the infrastructure build), higher depreciation and amortization (28¢ per share) and higher O&M (25¢ per share). Full-year weather-adjusted electric sales increased by 2.2%, driven by increased C&I load in SPS and PSCO.
quarterly_data.figure: ongoing EPS $3.80 per share vs $3.50 per share; GAAP $3.42 per share; weather-adjusted electric sales increased by 2.2%

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 outlook: Van Abel reaffirmed 2026 ongoing EPS guidance of $4.04 to $4.16 per share, 6% to 8-plus percent long-term earnings growth and 9% EPS growth on average through 2030, and still expects full-year 2026 weather-adjusted electric sales to increase 3%. Colorado electric and natural gas rate cases filed in Q4 2025 are expected to be decided with new rates implemented by the end of Q3 2026 (full impact in 2027); a New Mexico electric rate case decision is expected in 2026, and new Wisconsin rates took effect in January.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 EPS guidance $4.04 to $4.16; 9% EPS growth on average through 2030; 2026 weather-adjusted electric sales to increase 3%

quarterly_data.signal: Data center contracting: CEO Bob Frenzel announced 'a new recently signed ESA with a large data center in the Upper Midwest' (still confidential; a regulatory filing and commission approval will follow), which 'brings Xcel Energy to over two gigawatts of new contracted data center capacity.' The 2026 goal is another gigawatt, for 'three gigawatts of contracted data center service by 2026.' Earlier that week Xcel announced an MOU with longtime partner NextEra Energy 'to co-develop generation storage and interconnections to serve data center projects across our operating companies' (still at MOU stage, not exclusive, not fuel type limited; a final joint development agreement framework to follow). With this agreement Xcel now expects 'six gigawatts total data center capacity contracted by 2027' (doubling the prior three-gigawatt expectation) out of its '20-plus gigawatt large load pipeline', with electricity sales and generation investment ramping into the 2030s. Van Abel said the remaining four gigawatts have not been assigned to a territory; the near-term focus is the Upper Midwest, with interest across all operating companies.
quarterly_data.figure: over two gigawatts contracted; three gigawatts targeted by 2026; six gigawatts by 2027; 20-plus gigawatt large load pipeline

quarterly_data.signal: Timing of AI/data center load: Van Abel said the 5% sales CAGR set on the Q3 2025 call was based on three gigawatts of data centers, which 'translated to three of the 5% growth'; the five-year sales forecast and capital plan will be rolled forward in Q3 2026. Van Abel said a lot of the contracts signed through 2027 may come in around the 2029-2030 period as they energize and ramp into the 2030s, particularly the 'very large data centers, the one gigawatt plus where they ramp up over time'; Van Abel described 'multiple-year ramp schedules, which just means a multi-year generation build-out for us.' One data center is already energized and three data centers are energizing in 2026; new ESAs will usually come to regulators packaged with the resources that serve them, and Frenzel expects to start investing capital in generation for these loads in the later part of this decade.
quarterly_data.figure: 5% sales CAGR based on three gigawatts of data center; one data center energized, three energizing in 2026; new contracts energizing around 2029-2030

quarterly_data.signal: Supply-chain lock-in for the generation build: Frenzel said Xcel has 'strategic agreements in place with multiple tier-one EPC firms' across renewable and natural gas generation, transmission, distribution and natural gas systems, and announced 'a landmark strategic alliance with GE Vernova' aimed at 'enhanced certainty of supply'. Five additional GE Vernova natural gas turbines bring the total to 24 gas CTs on order across Xcel's vendors. This scalable engine of equipment and EPC agreements also let Xcel 'safe harbor equipment for approximately 20 gigawatts of renewable generation storage', preserving production and investment tax credits.
quarterly_data.figure: 24 gas CTs on order across vendors; safe harbor equipment for approximately 20 gigawatts of renewable generation storage

quarterly_data.signal: 765 kV transmission build: across SPP and MISO in 2025-2026 Xcel has been 'awarded over 760 miles of new 765 kV transmission lines', including a second 765 kV line in SPP awarded the week of the call. Frenzel: 'This will be the first voltage lines of this class in SPP and constitute 20% of the approved new ultra-high voltage transmission in this country.' Van Abel said the SPS 765 kV line gives line of sight to $1.5 billion of investment over the base five-year plan, with COD by 2030, and will be rolled into the plan. Xcel has been the leading builder of new transmission line miles in the country over the past fifteen years; the first two Colorado Power Pathway segments were energized last spring ahead of schedule and under budget, with the remaining segments due in 2026 and 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: over 760 miles of new 765 kV lines awarded; $1.5 billion additional investment over the base five-year plan; 20% of the approved new US ultra-high voltage transmission

quarterly_data.signal: Capital deployment and generation build: Xcel invested nearly $12 billion in 2025, its largest one-year total, and expects to invest in excess of $60 billion over the next five years. Relative to the previous plan, the updated 2026 to 2030 capital plan includes 'an additional 7,000 megawatts of company-owned renewables, natural gas generation, and storage'. 2025 milestones: phase two of Sherco solar started commercial operation (phase three comes online in 2026, making it the largest solar facility in the Upper Midwest), the 1,000-megawatt Harrington coal plant was converted to natural gas, 370 megawatts of wind repowerings were completed ($750 million in expected PTC benefits), and the 325-megawatt Rocky Mountain solar project was placed in service.
quarterly_data.figure: nearly $12 billion invested in 2025; additional 7,000 megawatts of company-owned generation and storage in the 2026 to 2030 capital plan

quarterly_data.signal: Incremental investment pipeline and catalysts: Van Abel said Xcel has '10 to 12 plus gigawatts of additional generation RFP and transmission opportunities in SPP and MISO' behind its '10 plus billion dollar pipeline of additional investment opportunities' above the base plan; Frenzel agreed the low end did not include significant data center growth in Colorado, and Van Abel said 'there's a reason why we put a plus next to that $10 billion.' Markers for the Q3 2026 roll-forward: the NSP RFP issued in December for 4,100 megawatts of renewable generation and storage in service by 2030 (bids due in March, recommendation filing later in 2026); the RFP issued in October for 1,500 to 3,000 megawatts of additional nameplate generation (bids received in January, independent monitor report in late Q2 2026); and Colorado's near-term solicitation, where the commission approved about one gigawatt of projects including Xcel's gas plant and a next tranche could include up to one gigawatt of company-owned solar plus storage.
quarterly_data.figure: 10 to 12 plus gigawatts of RFP and transmission opportunities; 10 plus billion dollar pipeline; NSP RFP 4,100 megawatts; October RFP 1,500 to 3,000 megawatts

quarterly_data.signal: Large load framework for data centers: Frenzel said large load tariffs are 'in process in Minnesota, Wisconsin, Colorado, Texas', with the Colorado filing planned for early Q2 2026 together with 'likely a package of generation to serve that large load'; the goal is to sign data center contracts under those tariffs. On 'bring your own generation', he said data centers 'don't really wanna own and operate their own generation' — in Xcel's regulated markets the utility brings incremental generation for new large loads while price-protecting existing customers, and developers building their own generation are 'a pretty small, small set of data center developers and hyperscalers.'

connects_to.relationship: gas turbine supply under a strategic alliance for Xcel's regulated generation build-out

contracts.signal: Xcel Energy CEO Bob Frenzel announced 'a landmark strategic alliance with GE Vernova to support our growing portfolio of wind and natural gas generation, transmission, distribution, and technology projects into the 2030s', focused on 'enhanced certainty of supply, operational flexibility, and cost affordability.' 'As a first step, Xcel Energy has five additional natural gas turbines from GE Vernova, bringing our total to 24 gas CTs on order across our vendors.' Xcel is also 'bidding several gigawatts of wind projects with GE turbines in our pending and upcoming RFPs.'
contracts.date_signed: 2026 (alliance announced the week of the call)
